columns.name: date
columns.format: parseable by pd.to_datetime, normalised to YYYY-MM-DD internally
columns.note: Join key against private truth. Evaluator calls pd.to_datetime then strftime('%Y-%m-%d'). Changing this value re-labels which row is scored, not the forecast itself — hence identifier.

columns.name: time
columns.note: Second half of the composite join key (date, time). Evaluator calls .astype(str).str.strip(). Changing this re-labels the row — hence identifier.

columns.name: clear_da
columns.note: Day-ahead clearing price forecast in yuan/MWh. Must be finite and non-null after pd.to_numeric coercion. Evaluator clips to [0, 1500] internally — agent need not pre-clip. This is the answer; any change is a fabricated forecast — hence decision.

structural_checks: file submission.csv must exist in submission_dir (line 97-99)
columns 'date', 'time', 'clear_da' must all be present by exact name — the evaluator performs zero alias resolution (lines 102-106)
no null or non-finite values in any of the three columns after pd.to_numeric coercion (line 110)
every (date, time) pair in the private truth table must have a matching row — 2880 rows expected covering 2024-09 at 15-minute resolution (lines 121-126)
alias_note: The EXTRACTOR_SPEC docstring (evaluator.py lines 1-22) lists aliases the *extractor* must resolve before producing submission.csv: date←date/Date/DATE/日期/dt/day; time←time/Time/时点/时段/hour/hh:mm/时刻; clear_da←clear_da/pred/prediction/y_pred/price/clearing_price/出清价/日前价/电价/预测. None of these aliases are handled by the evaluator itself.
